title: Q-CONSOLE-SESSION-1: console agent proposes a code change as a fleet task (fresh code, audited, undoable)
body:
**Owner:** executor
**Trigger:** executor tick, driver order
**Done check:** grep:dashboard/agent.js::propose_change
**Status:** closed

Console agent parity (owner directive 2026-11-14: the command line should work like a top-tier server-side coding agent; CONSOLE-AGENT-1 shipped the read, orchestrate and audited-change agent).

The console agent reads data and runs registered commands, and `delegate` and `dispatch` hand code work to the fleet and GitHub Actions. It cannot yet turn a plain-English change request into a code change itself. Add a `propose_change` tool to `dashboard/agent.js`, available only with a fresh code: it writes a fleet task whose body is the request, the paths the agent read, acceptance criteria and a closing probe (through the existing `note`/`delegate` path, so it is audited and undoable), and the executor opens the pull request, which the merge lane takes. The agent then reports the task id and how to follow it. Test with the scripted model in `dashboard/test/agent.test.mjs`: refused without a fresh code, a task row and an audit row with one, undo removes the row.

A container with a shell is a separate scope decision (a new capability and a new attack surface) and is not part of this item.

size: M

**Closing probe:** grep:dashboard/agent.js::propose_change.

**Disposition:** shelved (ttl, 2026-11-21T18:12:26Z, DISPOSE-1)

**Evidence:** open 157.0 hours (limit 6 hours) and no loop closed it (SLA-8H-1). Its closing probe still runs on every fleet pass and records `fixed` when it passes; the executor retries it when its open queue is empty (every 30 days at most).
